questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The little boy called up his best friend on his birthday.

options.text: His best friend has been called up by the little boy on his birthday.
His best friend was called up by the little boy on his birthday.
His best friend is called up by the little boy on his birthday.
His best friend was being called up by the little boy on his birthday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**His best friend was called up by the little boy on his birthday.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 
__
 
• In passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The passive sentence is formed using the auxiliary verb "to be" + past participle of the main verb.
 
• In this sentence, "his best friend" is the object of the active sentence, so it becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• "Called up" is the main verb, and its past participle form is "called up."
 
• Therefore, the correct passive sentence is:
 
 
• "His best friend was called up by the little boy on his birthday."
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1**: "His best friend has been called up by the little boy on his birthday." This is also in passive voice, but the use of "has been" instead of "was" is incorrect because the action happened in the past, not the present perfect.
 
• **Option 3**: "His best friend is called up by the little boy on his birthday." This is in present tense, not past tense, so it is not correct for this sentence.
 
• **Option 4**: "His best friend was being called up by the little boy on his birthday." This is in passive voice, but the use of "being" implies that the action was ongoing or in progress, which is not specified in the original sentence.

questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. Through a subtle analysis, Woolf raises certain concerns regarding discrimination against women in a male-dominated society.

B. It's also against the need for freedom of expression in women, and the right to human dignity and equality.

C .In 'Shakespeare's Sister', Virginia Woolf explores the plight of women in society in England during the 15th and 16th centuries.

D. It is against the denial of education to the girl-child and violence against women.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**CADB.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• **The subject of the passage is regarding Virginia Woolf's 'Shakespeare's Sister."**

 
 
• **Thus, we will place the sentence C at the beginning of the passage.**
 
 
 
• Virginia Woolf's essay 'Shakespeare's Sister' explores the challenges faced by women in a male-dominated society.
 
 
• Thus, sentence A will follow sentence C in the passage.
 
 
 
• Further in sentence D, Woolf's analysis raises concerns about discrimination against women, denial of education to girls, and violence against women.
 
• The essay also highlights the need for freedom of expression, human dignity, and equality for women through sentence B.
 
• The sentences can be arranged in the order C-A-D-B to form a coherent paragraph.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 4**.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Who stole my tickets?

options.text: My tickets was stolen by whom?
My tickets got stolen by who?
By whom were my tickets stolen?
My tickets were stolen by who?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**By whom were my tickets stolen?**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in the active voice with the subject "who" performing the action of stealing.
 
• **To convert it into passive voice, the object "my tickets" becomes the subject and the verb "stole" is changed to its past participle form "stolen."**
 
• **The doer of the action, "who," is now introduced with the preposition "by" as the agent of the passive sentence.**
 
• The passive sentence structure is "object + auxiliary verb (be) + past participle verb + by + agent."
 
• Thus, the correct statement would be:
 
 
• By whom were my tickets stolen?
 
 

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Option 1**, "My tickets was stolen by whom?" is incorrect because the verb "was" does not agree with the subject "tickets" which is plural.
 
• **Option 2**, "My tickets got stolen by who?" is incorrect because it uses the colloquial expression "got stolen" instead of the correct passive form "were stolen."
 
• **Option 4**, "My tickets were stolen by who?" is grammatically correct but does not use the passive voice correctly as it does not invert the subject-object relationship.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Darshan wished he hadn't / went to the theme park / in the first place.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**went to the theme park**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the error lies in the part "went to the theme park."
 
• **The correct verb tense to use in this sentence is "hadn't gone" instead of "hadn't went".**
 
• **When “had” is used as a helping or auxiliary verb, it is followed by a main verb in the past participle tense (V3). **
 
• "Went" is the past tense form of "go."
 
• On the other hand, "gone" is the past participle form that should be used with "hadn't".
 
• Therefore, the error is in the third part of the sentence.
 
• The correct sentence will be: Darshan wished he hadn't gone to the theme park in the first place.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 3**.
